questions.question: Why is it important to explicitly flush the standard output stream (stdout) immediately after writing a shell prompt?
options: To clear the input buffer of any trailing newline characters
To allocate memory for the upcoming user command string
To ensure the prompt is immediately displayed when output is buffered
To reset the terminal color codes back to default values

questions.question: When reading input in a Go REPL using bufio.Scanner, what is the primary advantage over directly using fmt.Scan?
options: bufio.Scanner automatically executes any shell commands it reads
bufio.Scanner safely reads arbitrarily long lines separated by newlines, including spaces
fmt.Scan cannot be used with standard input streams in Go
bufio.Scanner prevents buffer overflows by restricting input to 8 bytes

questions.question: How should a robust Read-Eval-Print Loop handle an EOF (End-Of-File) condition on standard input (e.g., when the user presses Ctrl+D)?
options: Break out of the REPL loop and terminate the program cleanly with exit code 0
Automatically restart the standard input stream and display an error warning
Ignore the EOF signal and wait indefinitely for a keyboard interrupt
Panic immediately to alert the operating system of an abnormal stream termination
